text: The following question stood in the name of  Dr Lim Wee Kiak –  1 To ask the Minister for Foreign Affairs (a) since the outbreak of the COVID-19 in China, how many Singaporeans have officially registered themselves with the Ministry; (b) to date, how many Singaporeans who returned to Singapore have been infected with the virus; and (c) how many registered Singaporeans are still in China and how many are infected.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Whilst we do not track the movements of Singaporeans overseas, it is reasonable for us to assume that a number of them would have since visited Mainland China and left, or returned to Singapore, at least for the time being.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We believe that the actual number of Singaporeans there is much higher.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Therefore, this is as good a time as any for me to remind all Singaporeans overseas to please eRegister with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In particular, given the ongoing COVID-19 outbreak in China and in many other countries, we urge Singaporeans to eRegister with us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It enables us to stay in touch with them, to contact them and to provide for any emergency or urgent messages, as well as for them to stay in contact with us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should also add, as the Minister in charge of the Smart Nation initiative, that we have now made it even easier than ever before to eRegister using SingPass Mobile.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our Embassy in Beijing and our Consulates-General in Shanghai, Guangzhou, Chengdu and Xiamen maintain close contact with the Singapore community in mainland China.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Any Singaporean there who is in need of consular assistance can approach my colleagues in those Missions at any time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It helped that many of them were eRegistered, which made it much easier for us to contact them and to make the arrangements to bring them home.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Upon their return to Singapore, they were placed on quarantine in Government Quarantine Facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will have to continue to keep watch on the viral outbreak in China and, indeed, in many other places of the world as the situation unfolds.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the meantime, life must go on, even as we take additional precautions and make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am confident that we will get through this crisis as one united people.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Is it a matter of concern, or are we just assuming that if they do not want to come back, they do not want to come back and so, let them decide on their own?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There are multiple reasons that they have offered.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There were others – perhaps not so much now but in the earlier phase of the crisis – who were worried even about travelling, making the journey to Wuhan, and therefore, decided that they would stay in place.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think every family will have its own unique reasons.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The key point is this: we will remain in touch; we will do our best to help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It would also help if they eRegistered with us because that gives us an immediate, direct line to them and, similarly, for them to us.
